currentContext.strategies: Deepen a differentiated multi-brand portfolio (Tanishq, Zoya, Mia by Tanishq, CaratLane, Damas, beYon in jewellery; Titan, Raga, Edge, Xylys, Sonata, Fastrack, Nebula in watches) to capitalise on premiumisation and formalisation of the industry|Expand retail network into high-potential Tier 2 & 3 cities and dense jewellery corridors using a mix of franchise-led and FOCO/Company-operated store formats|Scale international presence in line with diaspora demand, including US store additions and integration of the acquired Damas Jewellery business in the GCC|Deepen customer trust and engagement through transparency-led initiatives such as the Gold Exchange Programme and industry-first Diamond Expertise Centres|Entry into new adjacent categories, including lab-grown diamond jewellery under the 'beYon' brand and lower-karat (18kt/14kt) jewellery to broaden affordability amid elevated gold prices|Leverage AI, ML, IoT 4.0 and robotics, and continued digital/omnichannel investment, to build a smarter, more efficient supply chain and customer engagement platform|Continue Retail Transformation programmes across Tanishq, EyeCare and Watches to modernise store formats and improve conversion|Dividend of Rs 15 per equity share (face value Rs 1) for FY26 was put up for shareholder approval at the AGM (27th July 2026). The Board's governance philosophy commits the Company to directing energies and resources towards enhancing shareholder value while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders, aiming to drive sustainable, inclusive and responsible growth.
currentContext.expansion: Titan's expansion during FY26 was largely retail-network and technology-led rather than greenfield-capacity led. The Watches Division grew its network to 1,292 stores (743 Titan World, 288 Helios, 252 Fastrack, 9 Helios Luxe). Tanishq's Retail Transformation programme took its network to 528 stores, including renovation of 150 stores, addition of 57 new stores and rationalisation of 109 under-performing stores, plus the first Rivaah Wedding Lounge in New Delhi. CaratLane added 50 stores (current count 378, plus 12 Shaya stores) including two in the US (New Jersey, Dallas). Mia by Tanishq expanded to 292 stores across 100+ towns. Zoya expanded to 13 exclusive boutiques across 9 Indian cities. Internationally, the Company acquired a 67% stake in Damas Jewellery (through wholly owned subsidiary Titan Holdings International FZCO), adding an established GCC store network, and plans to add four more US stores. On manufacturing/technology: the Company deployed Industrial IoT in the Case Machine Shop and digital dashboards with end-to-end machine connectivity in the Module Plant's Gears Shop; the EyeCare manufacturing unit added 3D printing for rapid prototyping, injection moulding technology for in-house TR frame production, and Lens Remote Edging Technology adding capacity of 1,000 lenses/day with robotic edging accuracy of +/-0.05mm; EyeCare ISCM achieved JUSE Level 5 certification for World Class Manufacturing implementation. On renewable/energy infrastructure, the Company commissioned approximately 910 kW of onsite/rooftop solar capacity across manufacturing locations (200 kW at Watches Hosur, 460 kW at Watches Coimbatore, 100 kW at Watches Pantnagar, 150 kW at EyeCare Chikkaballapur, taking EyeCare's total solar capacity to 511 kW), alongside a 5-stage RO water-recovery system at Hosur (commissioned November 2025, achieving up to 95% water recovery) and multiple water-conservation/ecological-restoration projects (e.g., Vaaranavanam 50-hectare habitat restoration, Siruthuli stream restoration in Coimbatore).

risks.risk: Data privacy across all business operations
risks.note: Probability of breach of customer/employee Sensitive Personal Information in violation of country-specific privacy regulations; mitigated via privacy impact assessments, a data privacy framework, privacy-enhancing technologies and independent benchmarking.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk, particularly customs duties on gold
risks.note: The Company operates in a regulated environment; the Jewellery business is sensitive to changes in customs duties on gold and other precious materials and other fiscal measures that directly influence input costs, pricing and demand, which could affect margins and consumer behaviour especially in value-sensitive segments.

risks.risk: Geopolitical risk and gold price / currency volatility
risks.note: Ongoing global conflicts and geopolitical tensions contribute to volatility in gold prices, currency movements and macroeconomic conditions, which may influence consumer sentiment and demand patterns especially in discretionary segments, and can impact supply chains and input costs across markets including the Middle East and the United States.

Potential loss of sensitive data or disruption to operations due to cyber-attack or hardware/software failure, compromise of customer data, or defacement of the Company's website/social media profiles.

risks.risk: Data security leakage from third-party agencies
risks.note: Use of third-party agencies for business activities creates a probability of loss of business-sensitive and customer data managed by those third parties.

risks.risk: Ongoing West Asia conflict impacting FY27 outlook
risks.note: The Company enters FY27 amid an external environment expected to remain volatile, with geopolitical uncertainties, particularly the ongoing conflict in West Asia, potentially impacting consumer sentiment, supply chains and input costs including precious metals and gemstones.

one-line thesis: Strong Q4 top-line growth driven by gold price inflation and exchange program momentum, but margins under pressure from product mix shifts and unallocated employee rewards; Damas integration losses and transfer pricing adjustments distort standalone profitability, while new initiatives like gemstone jewellery and 14/18-carat offerings aim to sustain long-term growth despite macro volatility.
financial scorecard: revenue: +18% YoY (consolidated); EBITDA/margin: 11.2% (-120 bps YoY, impacted by gold mix + ₹120cr unallocated rewards); PAT (rptd): ₹1,420cr (-15% YoY due to Damas loss + ₹120cr reward); PAT (normalized): ₹1,900cr (+12% YoY); order book: N/A; net debt: ₹1,850cr (up ₹400cr YoY from inventory build + Damas capex)
guidance: revenue growth: 15-20% CAGR (3-5yr); margin: no specific FY27 guidance, sustainability tied to gold stability; order inflow: Damas to be disclosed post-integration; capex/commissioning: ₹1,200cr FY27 (retail expansion, TEAL automation, CaratLane ERP, beYon scaling)
segment / subsidiary detail: Jewellery: 85% revenue, 18% YoY growth; Tanishq buyer growth +8% in Q4; CaratLane: 22-23% growth despite ERP disruption; Watches: analog 85% of segment, +16% YoY; Eyecare: steady; Damas: ₹82cr Q4 loss (GCC disruption), full-year profitable; Bullion: inventory optimization, no profit; beYon: 2 stores, targeting 10-12; Taneira: under review, focus on sub-₹10k segment; TEAL: strong growth in aerospace/defense; Hues: new gemstone line, ₹40k-₹10L range
growth verticals / optionality: beYon expansion to 10-12 stores; Hues gemstone collection scaling; TEAL capture in China+1 manufacturing; Damas retail conversion to Tanishq in GCC; CaratLane ERP stabilization; 14/18-carat gold penetration; Grammage Purchase Plan redemption ramp-up
margins & cost dynamics: Margin pressure from gold price inflation (10-20 bps erosion); offset by lightweight jewellery, 14/18-carat mix shift, overhead control; exchange program investment sustained; no major discounting; margin sustainability hinges on gold price stability
capex / expansion: ₹1,200cr planned for FY27: ₹500cr retail expansion (Tanishq, beYon, CaratLane); ₹300cr TEAL automation; ₹200cr CaratLane ERP & tech; ₹100cr Damas integration; ₹100cr eyecare & Hues R&D
capital allocation: Prioritizing growth capex (retail, TEAL, tech); dividend policy unchanged; no buyback announced; Damas minority stake acquisition possible in 4 years if successful; cash flow generation remains key
risks & watch-items: Gold price volatility; GCC geopolitical instability; CaratLane ERP execution risk; margin compression if gold rises further; beYon scalability; Taneira turnaround delay; regulatory changes in gold import; competitive discounting
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term 15-20% growth, optimistic on gold category resilience, pragmatic on margin pressures, transparent on one-offs (Damas, rewards, transfer pricing), proactive on innovation (Hues, exchange, 14/18-carat)
non-obvious takeaways: ₹120cr unallocated reward is a one-off, not recurring; transfer pricing adjustment of ₹80cr is structural, not a loss; Damas loss is primarily from GCC disruption, not integration failure; Hues gemstone line targets design seekers, not just entry-level; CaratLane’s Q4 slowdown was ERP-driven, not demand-driven; bullion sales are inventory liquidity, not profit center

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Premiumisation remains a key structural driver of growth across the Titan, Raga, Edge and Xylys watch brands and across jewellery price bands
- Formalisation of the jewellery industry is increasing competitive intensity
- Elevated and volatile gold prices moderated demand at lower price points (single-digit buyer growth) while driving strong growth in higher price bands and studded jewellery
- Structural shift toward analog watches expected to continue in FY27, with the premium segment (above Rs 25,000) supported by the European Free Trade Association trade deal on Swiss watches
- International markets expected to remain dynamic, with cautious optimism in the United States (despite elevated tariffs necessitating supply chain redesign) and watchfulness in the Middle East given geopolitical conditions
- Eyewear industry has a large underserved market for vision correction in India (an estimated 700 million requiring correction, only about 250 million currently addressed), with structural tailwinds from increased screen time, eye health awareness and premiumisation
- Jewellery demand supported by favourable demographics and jewellery's continued relevance as a store of value in India, though short-term demand fluctuations may persist

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin pressure from gold price inflation (10-20 bps erosion); offset by lightweight jewellery, 14/18-carat mix shift, overhead control; exchange program investment sustained; no major discounting; margin sustainability hinges on gold price stability

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Titan's expansion during FY26 was largely retail-network and technology-led rather than greenfield-capacity led. The Watches Division grew its network to 1,292 stores (743 Titan World, 288 Helios, 252 Fastrack, 9 Helios Luxe). Tanishq's Retail Transformation programme took its network to 528 stores, including renovation of 150 stores, addition of 57 new stores and rationalisation of 109 under-performing stores, plus the first Rivaah Wedding Lounge in New Delhi. CaratLane added 50 stores (current count 378, plus 12 Shaya stores) including two in the US (New Jersey, Dallas). Mia by Tanishq expanded to 292 stores across 100+ towns. Zoya expanded to 13 exclusive boutiques across 9 Indian cities. Internationally, the Company acquired a 67% stake in Damas Jewellery (through wholly owned subsidiary Titan Holdings International FZCO), adding an established GCC store network, and plans to add four more US stores. On manufacturing/technology: the Company deployed Industrial IoT in the Case Machine Shop and digital dashboards with end-to-end machine connectivity in the Module Plant's Gears Shop; the EyeCare manufacturing unit added 3D printing for rapid prototyping, injection moulding technology for in-house TR frame production, and Lens Remote Edging Technology adding capacity of 1,000 lenses/day with robotic edging accuracy of +/-0.05mm; EyeCare ISCM achieved JUSE Level 5 certification for World Class Manufacturing implementation. On renewable/energy infrastructure, the Company commissioned approximately 910 kW of onsite/rooftop solar capacity across manufacturing locations (200 kW at Watches Hosur, 460 kW at Watches Coimbatore, 100 kW at Watches Pantnagar, 150 kW at EyeCare Chikkaballapur, taking EyeCare's total solar capacity to 511 kW), alongside a 5-stage RO water-recovery system at Hosur (commissioned November 2025, achieving up to 95% water recovery) and multiple water-conservation/ecological-restoration projects (e.g., Vaaranavanam 50-hectare habitat restoration, Siruthuli stream restoration in Coimbatore).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified brand portfolio spanning luxury to mass-market price points across jewellery, watches and eyewear
- Large owned and franchised retail network (3,603 stores; 46 lakh sq ft retail area) with omnichannel presence
- Ethical/responsible sourcing framework with over 90% of vendors sustaining a 'Standard' 4P (People, Place, Process, Planet) rating and 100% ethical diamond sourcing via the Titan Supplier Engagement Protocol
- Trusted brand equity rooted in Tata Group heritage, reinforced by initiatives such as the Gold Exchange Programme and Diamond Expertise Centres
- Premiumisation-led product innovation pipeline (e.g., in-house tourbillon movements, Wandering Hour, PhotoFusion lenses) across categories

risks.body: Gold price volatility; GCC geopolitical instability; CaratLane ERP execution risk; margin compression if gold rises further; beYon scalability; Taneira turnaround delay; regulatory changes in gold import; competitive discounting

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: ₹120cr unallocated reward is a one-off, not recurring; transfer pricing adjustment of ₹80cr is structural, not a loss; Damas loss is primarily from GCC disruption, not integration failure; Hues gemstone line targets design seekers, not just entry-level; CaratLane’s Q4 slowdown was ERP-driven, not demand-driven; bullion sales are inventory liquidity, not profit center

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen a differentiated multi-brand portfolio (Tanishq, Zoya, Mia by Tanishq, CaratLane, Damas, beYon in jewellery; Titan, Raga, Edge, Xylys, Sonata, Fastrack, Nebula in watches) to capitalise on premiumisation and formalisation of the industry
- Expand retail network into high-potential Tier 2 & 3 cities and dense jewellery corridors using a mix of franchise-led and FOCO/Company-operated store formats
- Scale international presence in line with diaspora demand, including US store additions and integration of the acquired Damas Jewellery business in the GCC
- Deepen customer trust and engagement …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Damas is now consolidated — Signature Jewellery Holding Limited, Dubai (the holding company for the Damas Jewellery entities) is held 67%, with Damas Income and EBIT included post acquisition from Q4FY26, making international figures not strictly comparable to last year.
- [Regulation] Customs duty on gold rose steeply from 6% to 15% effective May 13, 2026; the deck quantifies a resulting benefit in realization of ₹386 crores for Tanishq/Mia/Zoya and ₹21 crores for CaratLane in the quarter, and presents duty-adjusted EBIT alongside reported EBIT for both.
- [Group structure] As of 30th June 2026 Titan Company Limited holds 100% of TEAL, CaratLane Trading Private Limited, TCL North America Inc, Titan Holdings International FZCO (Dubai) and Titan Commodity Trading Limited, with TEAL USA Inc. and StudioC Inc. (USA) under TEAL, and Titan Global Retail LLC (Dubai), Titan International QFZ LLC (Qatar), Titan Watch Company Limited (Hong Kong) and the 67%-held Signature Jewellery Holding Limited (Dubai) below the Dubai holding company.
- [Leadership] Management commentary is signed by Mr. Ajoy Chawla, Managing Director, who cites navigating gold prices, the sharp change in duty structure and geopolitical headwinds across international operations.
- [One-time item] The Watches business "had one-time gains resulting from inventory revaluation that had a positive EBIT margin impact"; adjusting for this, the deck states EBIT was ₹275 crores at 17.8% margin.
- [History] The journey slide records incorporation in 1984, the jewellery facility and Golden Harvest Scheme, Gold Plus and Tanishq, Precision Engineering (PED) which was later demerged, Titan E-Commerce, and the acqui-hire of HUG Innovations, with revenue rising from ₹354 crores through ₹2,996 crores and ₹11,343 crores to ₹76,078 crores in FY26 (individual year-to-value bindings other than the FY26 figure are not recoverable from the extract).
- [Recognition] The Titan Zero Hour 500M timepiece set a Guinness World Record for the world's deepest underwater product photoshoot at 52.1 metres (170.9 ft), and the feature film 'Made in India: A Titan Story' aired on Amazon Prime Video; Titan Watches earned Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) nominations for Edge Ultra Slim and The Wandering Meteor.
